messages.author: dd68a26ecdacedb8
messages.subject: Re: polar graph
parts:
This example should get you going. It's based on p. 199 of the excellent "R Graphic Cookbook" by Winston Cheng.

Install the the gcookbook package to your R environment. Then:

require(gcookbook)
myPlot <- ggplot(wind, aes(x=DirCat, fill=SpeedCat)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth=max(30), origin=0) +
    coord_polar() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,360))
myPlot

wind is a data set that comes with the gcookbook package. I'd hack it by creating a couple of new variables and building something similar to what you want using an enhanced wind, then port it to your data.

-Phil
